open_issues.text: Protocol addition chosen at detail level: append accepts an optional seed_state_version. The hub's seed of an empty generation is appended as the log's first record (origin server), and the backend refuses it with 409 collaboration_seed_conflict (the problem code is reused) once the generation has a record or a checkpoint, or the state version moved. Without it, removing the v1 store (seed=true plus state_version precondition) would have lost both protections: two hubs seeding at once (duplicated content) and a REST update between load and seed (silently overwritten by the next checkpoint). The protocol section's append body did not list the field.

open_issues.text: Bug fixed along the way (D43 (4)): the P5.4 append path did not re-check the drive status under its locks, so an archive or deletion committed after CollaborationHub::open still let an append land; the v1 action checked it (assertUserWritable). UpdateLog::append now reads the drive status with a shared locking read under the drive lock that lock() takes (archived → 403 permission_denied, not active → 404), after the receipt lookup, so a committed retry still gets its receipt. HubDriveLifecycleTest proves it on sqlite; the pgsql liveness race tests were rewritten on append.

open_issues.impact: a server change on a hub without a connected writer is not saved until a writer appears (lost on kill)

open_issues.text: Server-origin credentials: append requires a room JWT (ResolveCollaborationCall), and the design's 'subject in the body' for server appends does not exist in P5.4. A server/direct change is appended with the token serverWrite() names or its origin's context.token, else with the current token of a writer connected to this hub (or the serverToken option). With no such writer, the record waits in the ledger, logged once (no_credentials), until a writer connects or shutdown. Nothing is dropped, but nothing is persisted either.

For P5.8: persistence.js exports replayLog(document, {checkpoint, tail}); with no checkpoint the tail's first record is the hub's seed, so the worker replays the tail onto an empty Y.Doc and must not seed from the lease's content (a leased generation always has records). retry.js withRetry and the ledger's send(entry) can be reused; backend.js has no lease or checkpoint call yet (post() is module-private).

For P5.9: /metrics and /readyz can read persistence.state() (mode, writes, protocolMismatch, rooms, ledger stats, oldestPendingMs) and ledger.stats() (appended, retries, failures, dropped, epochDropped, epochMismatches, pending, pendingBytes). ledger.flush() is the shutdown flush (race it with SHUTDOWN_FLUSH_MS). Still to add: a forced stop of writes (persistence.stopWrites() for mutation admission), the MAX_UPDATE_BYTES check before decoding (today an oversized envelope gets the backend's 413 as a nack). Unchanged so far: stopOnSignals is still true, /health still listens on 0.0.0.0, the flush cycle starts in boot() (persistence.start()).

For P5.12, the client contract chosen: connect with the provider parameters {protocol: 2}; without it the connection is read-only. Envelope = stateless JSON {t:'u', v:2, g, id, h, b}; replies {t:'ack', id, seq, g} with the id exactly as sent, {t:'nack', id, code, retry} and {t:'status', mode, writes}. Hub nack codes: invalid_envelope, invalid_update, forbidden, writes_stopped (retry:true), collaboration_update_mismatch, collaboration_epoch_mismatch, collaboration_protocol_mismatch, plus backend codes. Close codes: 4409 epoch_changed, 4404 document_gone, 4403 forbidden, 4001 token expired. 4422 store_refused is gone, but packages/vue still expects it.

open_issues.text: Assumptions about Hocuspocus 4.3 that could not be checked against its dist here: a client's sync update carries the Connection (or {source:'connection'}) as its transaction origin; a direct connection's transact origin is null, {source:'local'} or the DirectConnection; the Redis extension's origin is the extension instance (as p5-design says; the v2 string and {source:'redis'} are also recognised); onStateless, connected and onDisconnect (socketId) payload keys; setting connection.readOnly makes Hocuspocus drop a writer's sync writes. Unknown origins count as server changes, appended once and idempotent for Yjs, so a wrong guess costs a duplicate record, never a lost change.

open_issues.text: Detail choices (D44, detail level): durable mode counts the backend as unavailable while the last retry series was exhausted (or after a protocol mismatch), and the kept record probes it on every flush cycle. Default budgets: 64 MiB total, 8 MiB per room. A stopped writer is muted (connection.readOnly) and its envelopes are refused; it is not disconnected. The supported surface lost the Api class PersistCollaborationStateInput (surface.txt regenerated, i13 entry removed). The vaulter_collab_snapshot_duration_seconds histogram moved from the deleted v1 action to Checkpoint::publish (tier label).
